items.title: Adaptive Auto-Harness: Sustained Self-Improvement for Agentic System Deployment on Open-Ended Task Streams
items.summary: Adaptive Auto-Harness introduces a novel framework for deploying agentic systems on dynamic, open-ended task streams. The system decomposes performance gaps into evolution and adaptation losses, using a stateful multi-agent evolver and harness tree with solve-time routing. This enables sustained performance improvement across varying task types without retraining for new problems. The multi-agent architecture allows specialized agents to handle different task characteristics, while routing ensures efficient assignment. This work addresses critical challenges in deploying LLM-based agents at scale: maintaining performance as task distributions shift and new problem types emerge. The approach bridges static benchmarks and real-world deployment scenarios.
items.origSummary: Adaptive Auto-Harness framework addresses dynamic task streams by decomposing performance gaps into evolution and adaptation losses, utilizing a stateful multi-agent evolver and harness tree with solve-time routing for sustained performance improvement.
items.why: Multi-agent framework for dynamic agentic systems

items.title: A Multi-AI-agent Framework Enabling End-to-end Finite Element Analysis for Solid Mechanics Problems
items.summary: AbaqusAgent demonstrates a multi-agent framework powered by large language models that automates finite element analysis, converting natural language problem descriptions directly into executable simulations. The system achieves high success rates across diverse solid mechanics problems, eliminating manual model setup. By combining specialized agents, the framework handles complexity of translating physics-based requirements into computational code. This advancement makes complex engineering simulations accessible through natural language interfaces, reducing entry barriers. The approach shows how agentic LLM systems orchestrate domain-specific workflows, enabling researchers to describe problems in plain language while the system handles technical implementation details.
items.origSummary: AbaqusAgent is a multi-agent framework using large language models to automate finite element analysis by converting natural language instructions into executable simulations with high success rates across diverse solid mechanics problems.
items.why: LLM agents automate complex engineering simulations

items.title: Fast-tracking genetic leads to reverse cellular aging
items.summary: Researchers successfully use Co-Scientist, an LLM-based research agent, to identify novel factors that reverse cellular aging in human cells. By analyzing biological data and existing literature, the agent discovered previously uncharacterized rejuvenation pathways. This demonstrates Co-Scientist's capability to accelerate hypothesis generation in complex biological systems. Rather than requiring manual literature sifting, the agent integrates information across studies to identify promising intervention points. The success in discovering effective rejuvenation factors suggests LLM agents can dramatically compress timelines for basic biological discovery, particularly in aging research where understanding mechanisms remains challenging.
items.origSummary: Biologists use Co-Scientist to find novel factors that successfully rejuvenate human cells.
items.why: LLM agent discovers cellular aging reversal

items.title: Finding the molecular switches behind new infectious diseases
items.summary: Researcher Clare Bryant employs Co-Scientist to identify genetic triggers underlying emerging infectious diseases. The LLM-based agent systematically analyzes genomic and epidemiological data to pinpoint molecular factors driving disease emergence and transmission. By synthesizing information across disparate studies and datasets, Co-Scientist helps identify actionable genetic targets for intervention. This application demonstrates the agent's capacity to work across complex, multi-dimensional biological datasets to extract disease mechanisms. For pandemic preparedness, accelerating identification of genetic triggers in novel pathogens could enable faster vaccine and therapeutic development, making agentic systems critical for public health response.
items.origSummary: Clare Bryant uses Co-Scientist to identify genetic triggers in emerging infectious diseases.
items.why: LLM agent identifies genetic disease triggers

items.title: OmniOPD: Logit-Free On-Policy Distillation via Speculative Verification
items.summary: OmniOPD improves on-policy distillation for LLMs by using chunk-level semantic similarity rather than token-level logits, addressing fundamental limitations in knowledge transfer from teacher to student models. The semantic-similarity approach improves learning reliability and performance, particularly with black-box teachers. By focusing on meaning-level alignment rather than prediction probability distributions, OmniOPD reduces brittleness in token-level training. This technique applies directly to building smaller, efficient LLM agents retaining reasoning capabilities of larger models. The approach enables cost-effective deployment of agentic systems by allowing efficient students to inherit sophisticated reasoning from capable teachers.
items.origSummary: OmniOPD addresses limitations of standard On-Policy Distillation by using chunk-level semantic similarity instead of token-level logits, improving learning reliability and performance with black-box teachers.
items.why: Improved distillation for efficient LLM agents

items.title: Gemini for Science: AI experiments and tools for a new era of discovery
items.summary: Google DeepMind's Gemini for Science introduces specialized AI tools and experiments designed to expand scientific research capacity and precision. The platform provides LLM-based agents tailored for specific scientific domains, enabling researchers to accelerate discovery processes. By combining language models with domain-specific reasoning, Gemini for Science supports tasks from hypothesis generation to data interpretation. This toolkit represents industrial-scale deployment of LLM agents for research, demonstrating practical integration into scientific workflows. For researchers in protein structure analysis, climate modeling, and related fields, these tools augment traditional computational approaches, potentially accelerating scientific discovery across multiple domains.
items.origSummary: A collection of science tools and experiments to expand the scale and precision of scientific exploration.

items.title: Opening new paths in aging research
items.summary: Calico Life Sciences uses Co-Scientist to connect scattered findings across aging research literature and generate novel research leads. The LLM agent synthesizes insights from disparate studies to identify new hypotheses and intervention targets that individual researchers might miss. Aging research benefits particularly from this approach because knowledge distributes across specialized studies; Co-Scientist integrates this fragmented landscape into actionable directions. The agent's ability to extract patterns from unstructured scientific literature accelerates hypothesis generation, compressing months of review into rapid synthesis. This demonstrates how LLM agents serve as research accelerators in fields where integrating diverse knowledge sources is the bottleneck.
items.origSummary: Calico Life Sciences uses Co-Scientist to connect scattered findings and generate new leads in aging research.
items.why: LLM agent accelerates aging research discovery

items.title: Accelerating discovery of liver disease mechanisms
items.summary: Filippo Menolascina leverages Co-Scientist to identify novel liver disease treatments and explain treatment-response heterogeneity—why existing drugs help some patients but not others. By analyzing clinical and molecular data, the agent discovered previously unrecognized disease subtypes with distinct molecular drivers, enabling precision medicine approaches. This dual contribution illustrates how LLM agents accelerate mechanistic understanding in clinical research. Understanding which patients benefit from which treatments is critical for drug development and patient stratification. Co-Scientist's ability to synthesize complex multi-omics data with clinical outcomes demonstrates potential for personalized medicine applications across disease areas.
items.origSummary: Filippo Menolascina uses Co-Scientist to identify new liver disease treatments and explain why existing drugs only help certain patients.
items.why: LLM agent identifies novel disease treatments

items.title: Uniting biological toolkits for a new approach to ALS
items.summary: Co-Scientist facilitates collaboration between Boston Children's Hospital and MIT researchers exploring RNA-based treatments for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. The agent integrates biological knowledge from both institutions' labs, identifying promising RNA therapeutic strategies while accelerating cross-institutional coordination. ALS research has historically moved slowly relative to disease progression urgency; LLM agents accelerating hypothesis generation could compress timelines. By serving as a knowledge integrator understanding molecular biology and institutional research directions, Co-Scientist enables rapid collaboration and hypothesis refinement across laboratories. The approach demonstrates potential for agentic systems to catalyze progress in urgent rare diseases.
items.origSummary: Co-Scientist unites Boston Children’s Hospital and MIT’s labs to explore new RNA-based treatments for ALS.
items.why: LLM agent explores RNA-based ALS treatments

items.title: Mining triggers extensive additional deforestation in sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: Large-scale mining activities across sub-Saharan Africa trigger extensive deforestation of dense tropical forests, with particular intensity driven by energy transition minerals including cobalt. Mining's direct footprint is amplified by secondary forest loss in surrounding regions. Cobalt mining is emblematic: its boom reflects rising electric vehicle and battery demand, yet creates significant climate costs through forest loss undermining decarbonization goals. The analysis reveals tension between clean energy transitions and biodiversity conservation in resource-rich regions. Understanding these trade-offs is critical for climate policy; sourcing minerals more sustainably becomes essential to ensure energy transition actually reduces net emissions.
items.origSummary: Extensive mining activity leads to large-scale deforestation of dense tropical forests across sub-Saharan Africa, driven particularly by key energy transition minerals such as cobalt.

items.title: Earth’s east–west albedo symmetry
items.summary: A 25-year satellite analysis reveals Earth exhibits persistent east–west albedo asymmetry split at the 27°E meridian, with clear-sky albedo, cloud radiative effect, and open-ocean fraction exhibiting triple symmetry around this line. This long-term symmetry suggests persistent atmospheric and oceanic circulation features drive systematic differences in planetary reflectivity. Albedo—the fraction of incoming solar radiation Earth reflects—is a critical climate variable; persistent asymmetries affect global energy balance and climate forcing. The discovery may reveal underappreciated organizing principles in Earth's climate system. Understanding what maintains this asymmetry could improve climate models and inform how climate patterns respond to perturbations.
items.origSummary: Analysis of a 25-year satellite record shows that Earth has a persistent east–west albedo symmetry split at 27° E, with clear-sky albedo, cloud radiative effect and open-ocean fraction exhibiting a triple symmetry around this meridian.
items.why: Earth's climate system exhibits persistent asymmetry

items.title: A natural depsipeptide antibiotic binds the E-site of the bacterial ribosome
items.summary: Advanced fractionation methods identified manikomycin, a novel depsipeptide antibiotic from Streptomyces rimosus with previously uncharacterized mechanisms. Manikomycin binds the E-site of bacterial large ribosomal subunit, a binding site rarely exploited by antibiotics, providing fresh mechanisms for protein synthesis disruption. The discovery demonstrates that systematic screening still identifies antibiotics with novel scaffolds and mechanisms rather than merely rediscovering known drugs. Protein structure knowledge—particularly of the ribosome—enabled target identification. As antibiotic resistance rises, novel mechanisms like ribosomal E-site binding offer new therapeutic angles, though clinical potential requires further development.
items.origSummary: Improved fractionation strategies can identify antibiotics with previously unseen scaffolds and mechanisms, exemplified by manikomycin from Streptomyces rimosus, which acts by targeting the E-site of the bacterial large ribosomal subunit.
items.why: Novel antibiotic targets ribosomal protein structure
